title: Mara and the Vow
premise: Sebastian Halloran, a ghostwriter who has spent his career erasing himself from other people's stories, is hired anonymously to pen the memoirs of Vivian Cross—a publishing heiress and his oldest professional enemy. Neither knows the other's identity at first: their contract routes all correspondence through an intermediary, turning them into reluctant pen pals who slowly fall for the stranger on the other end of the letters. When Sebastian discovers he's been writing the woman he's come to love—and that her family built its empire on a betrayal documented in her own memoir—he must choose between delivering the manuscript that will destroy her or confessing everything. In the end, Vivian chooses truth over legacy, publishes the memoir under both their names, and Sebastian finally lets himself be seen; they meet face to face after the last train has already left, with nowhere either of them needs to be but together.
about_author: Wren Thornbury is the pseudonym of a former literary scout who spent a decade reading manuscripts in train stations and hotel lobbies before writing her own. She lives in a coastal town where the last ferry leaves at nine, and she has never once been on it.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He accepts an anonymous ghostwriting commission through his agent—generous pay, strict secrecy, correspondence only through a intermediary called Meridian. The emotional beat is weary resignation: another life to borrow, another self to bury.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Pressured by her board to publish a legacy memoir, Vivian resents hiring a ghost but agrees to write answers to her anonymous writer's questions. Her first reply is cold, guarded—but she finds herself lingering over one honest sentence about her mother.

chapters.title: A History of Small Wars
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He recognizes the memoir subject's voice from a disastrous shared panel years ago: this is Vivian Cross, who publicly humiliated him early in his career. He nearly quits, then stays—for the money, he tells himself. Beat: resentment sharpened into curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Digging through her late father's papers for material, she finds a sealed folder labeled with a name she doesn't recognize. She writes to her ghost asking whether some truths are better left unpublished. Beat: first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: The Intermediary
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A meeting with Meridian reveals odd rules: no names exchanged, deadlines non-negotiable, and a clause that the manuscript must include 'the Halloran matter'—a phrase that stops him cold. Beat: unease; someone is orchestrating this.

chapters.title: Two Strangers, One Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Both, coincidentally, miss the same last train from the city and share a delayed platform conversation without knowing each other's identity—an easy, startling intimacy neither can explain. Beat: the love story quietly begins.

chapters.title: Correspondence
chapters.summary: Epistolary chapter, both POVs via letters. Their exchanges turn playful, then vulnerable: favorite failures, regrets, the question 'who were you before you became useful?' Beat: falling in love with a voice.

chapters.title: The Halloran Matter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Researching the phrase, he uncovers that decades ago Vivian's father stole credit for a debut novel by a writer named Halloran—Sebastian's uncle, whose ruined career ended in obscurity. Beat: personal stake ignites; the enemy sharpens again.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Lies
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. She reads the sealed folder: proof her father plagiarized and buried a young writer. Her board wants it suppressed; her mother begs her to burn it. Beat: loyalty versus truth becomes her central war.

chapters.title: Deadlines
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Torn between exposing the Cross empire through the memoir and protecting the woman behind the letters, he writes two versions of the pivotal chapter—one damning, one merciful—and can't decide which to send. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Face Behind the Voice
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. At a publishing gala, she overhears a fragment of Sebastian's speech cadence—the cadence from the letters. She tests him with a quoted line; his reaction confirms it. Beat: recognition, fury, and something dangerously like relief.

chapters.title: Enemies, Properly Introduced
chapters.summary: Dual POV confrontation. Vivian confronts Sebastian privately; old wounds and new betrayals collide. She doesn't reveal what she knows about the letters; he doesn't reveal the Halloran file. Beat: a truce built entirely on mutual concealment.

chapters.title: Working Late
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Forced collaboration on the memoir brings them into close quarters; working sessions stretch past midnight. Professional sparring gives way to real tenderness. Beat: the romance surfaces despite everything.

chapters.title: What Vivian Knew
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. She rereads every letter, realizing the man she fell for and the man she hates are the same—and that she answered honestly anyway. She drafts a confession letter and deletes it. Beat: longing at war with pride.

chapters.title: Meridian's Hand
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He discovers Meridian is Vivian's board chair, who engineered the pairing hoping the memoir would sanitize—or weaponize—the Halloran scandal. Beat: the conspiracy widens; trust in every institution collapses.

chapters.title: The Leaked Chapter
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. The damning version of Sebastian's chapter leaks to the press; her family's name ignites. She assumes Sebastian betrayed her. Beat: heartbreak weaponized; the midpoint wound goes deep.

chapters.title: Last Train
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He traces the leak to Meridian, but Vivian won't take his calls. He boards the last train to her coastal estate to confess in person—and she isn't there. Beat: desperation; time visibly running out.

chapters.title: The Vow
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They find each other at the station platform where they once talked as strangers. Full confessions, both directions: the letters, the file, the leak. Vivian makes him vow to tell the whole truth in print—including his own name. Beat: climax; choice made.

chapters.title: Boardroom Fire
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Together they face the board, exposing Meridian's manipulation and refusing the sanitized manuscript. Vivian stakes her inheritance on publication. Beat: power confronted; corruption named and refused.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The memoir publishes under three names: Cross, Halloran, and the restored name of Sebastian's uncle. Reviews, reckonings, and a quiet visit to his uncle's grave with a finished book in hand. Beat: grief transmuted into restitution.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Months later, on the same platform, they deliberately let the final train leave without them. No contracts, no intermediaries, nothing left hidden between them. Beat: stillness; love chosen freely, identities fully claimed.

chapters.title: Mara and the Vow
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV epilogue. He begins his first novel under his own name, about a woman named Mara who kept a vow. Vivian reads the opening page over his shoulder and corrects his grammar. Beat: warm, wry resolution—the ghostwriter, finally visible.
